(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:越中国の式内社|名けたしんしや]] [[Category:一宮]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:越中国|社1]] [[Category:室町時代の建築]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:越中国の式内社|名けたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:越中国|社1]] [[Category:室町時代の建築]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

Keta Shrines|Keta Shrine (disambiguation)}} {{Refimprove|date=August 14, 2014 (Thu) 15:39 (UTC)}} {{Shinto shrine |Name = Keta Shrine |Image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), shaden.jpg|270px]]

(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:越中国の式内社|名けたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:越中国|社1]] [[Category:室町時代の建築]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

Keta Shrines|Keta Shrine (disambiguation)}} {{Refimprove|date=August 14, 2014 (Thu) 15:39 (UTC)}} {{Shinto shrine |Name = Keta Shrine |Image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), shaden.jpg|270px]]
Shrine buildings |Location = {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}} Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1 |Coordinates = {{Coord|36|48|0.8|N|137|2|39.5|E|region:JP-16|name=Keta Shrine|display=inline,title}} |Deities = {{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}}

Former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} |Founded = {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}})
(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:越中国の式内社|名けたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:越中国|社1]] [[Category:Architecture of Muromachi period]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

Keta Shrines|Keta Shrine (disambiguation)}} {{Refimprove|date=August 14, 2014 (Thu) 15:39 (UTC)}} {{Shinto shrine |Name = Keta Shrine |Image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), shaden.jpg|270px]]

Former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} |Founded = {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}})
(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:越中国の式内社|名けたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:Etchū Province]] [[Category:Architecture of Muromachi period]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

Keta Shrines|Keta Shrine (disambiguation)}} {{Refimprove|date=August 14, 2014 (Thu) 15:39 (UTC)}} {{Shinto shrine |Name = Keta Shrine |Image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), shaden.jpg|270px]]
Shrine buildings |Location = {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}} Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1 |Coordinates = {{Coord|36|48|0.8|N|137|2|39.5|E|region:JP-16|name=Keta Shrine|display=inline,title}} |Deities = {{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q276944|1=Ōkuninushi}}

Former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} |Founded = {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}})
(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:重要文化財 (建造物)]] [[Category:Etchū Province]] [[Category:Architecture of Muromachi period]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]

(also {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}})) |Main Hall = {{ill|lt=Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|WD=Q210684|lt=Sangen-sha nagare-zukuri|1=Nagare-zukuri}} |Other name = |Festival = {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}} |Rites = |Map = {{Location map|Japan Toyama|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.8|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.5|label=Keta Shrine|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}}}} [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), entrance.jpg|thumb|Shrine grounds entrance]] '''Keta Shrine''' (けたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|lt=Shinto shrine|Q845945|WD=Q845945|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|lt=Takaoka City|Q502988|WD=Q502988|1=Takaoka, Toyama}}, {{ill|lt=Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|WD=Q132929|1=Toyama Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}} ({{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}} of {{ill|lt=Etchū Province|Q906899|WD=Q906899|1=Etchū Province}}. Under the {{ill|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}. Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|lt=provincial capital|Q1629088|WD=Q1629088|1=Kokufu}} and {{ill|lt=provincial temple|Q1207757|WD=Q1207757|1=Provincial temple}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|lt=Etchū Sōja|Q1107129|WD=Q1107129|1=Sōja shrine}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.” === Enshrined deities === ; Principal deities * '''{{ill|lt=Ōkuninushi|Q276944|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|1=Ōkuninushi}}''' * '''{{ill|lt=Nunakawa-hime|UNKNOWN|lt=Nunakawa-hime-no-Mikoto}}''' ; Associated deities * {{ill|lt=Kukurihime-no-Kami|Q11619891|WD=Q11619891|lt=Kikuri-hime-no-Mikoto|1=Kukurihime}} * {{ill|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|WD=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|1=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}} === History === === Founding === According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|lt=transfer of a divided spirit|Q195793|WD=Q195793|lt=kanjō|1=Bunrei}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 1 ({{ill|lt=717|Q23532|WD=Q23532|1=717}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985. states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views. # {{ill|lt=Noto Province|Q1047671|WD=Q1047671|1=Noto Province}} separated from {{ill|lt=Echizen Province|Q1047144|WD=Q1047144|1=Echizen Province}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 ({{ill|lt=718|Q23534|WD=Q23534|1=718}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō|Q1199879|WD=Q1199879|1=Tenpyō}} 13 ({{ill|lt=741|Q23597|WD=Q23597|1=741}}), and then separated again in {{ill|lt=Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|WD=Q1346307|1=Tenpyō-hōji}} 1 ({{ill|lt=757|Q31135|WD=Q31135|1=AD 757}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown., from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|lt=Keta Taisha|Q11129340|WD=Q11129340|1=Keta Taisha}} of {{ill|lt=Hakui District|Q1130953|WD=Q1130953|1=Hakui District, Ishikawa}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). # *History of Takaoka City*Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959. suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|lt=provincial governor|Q1351234|WD=Q1351234|1=Kokushi (official)}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated. # *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986. states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki**Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.. Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|lt=Gyōki|Q1136664|WD=Q1136664|1=Gyōki}} in {{ill|lt=Yōrō|Q1373061|WD=Q1373061|1=Yōrō}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|lt=Empress Genshō|Q235343|WD=Q235343|1=Empress Genshō}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000. also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757). According to *Hakusan no Ki*, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|lt=Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|WD=Q349263|1=Emperor Shōmu}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya. In {{ill|lt=Enchō|Q1327274|WD=Q1327274|1=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|lt=927|Q30470|WD=Q30470|1=927}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|lt=Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|WD=Q11123261|1=Senior Third Rank}} in {{ill|lt=Enryaku|Q1373176|WD=Q1373176|1=Enryaku}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|lt=Engi|Q1374325|WD=Q1374325|1=Engi (era)}} 8 (908). Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|lt=Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|WD=Q9610964|1=Myōjin Taisha}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate. === From the medieval period onward === Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|lt=Maeda clan|Q578033|WD=Q578033|1=Maeda clan}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|lt=Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|WD=Q1970535|1=Shinbutsu bunri}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji. In {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|lt=1931|Q18782|WD=Q18782|1=1931}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|lt=National Treasure|Q1139795|WD=Q1139795|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} (later an {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}}). === Shrine grounds === [[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|lt=Important Cultural Property|Q1188622|WD=Q1188622|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}})]] The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture. Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|lt=Ōtomo Shrine (Takaoka City)|Q11432351|WD=Q11432351|1=Ōtomo Shrine}} dedicated to {{ill|lt=Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|WD=Q386308|1=Ōtomo no Yakamochi}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja. === Major festivals === Each year on {{ill|lt=April 18|Q2521|WD=Q2521|1=April 18}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years. === Cultural properties === === Important Cultural Properties (National designation) === * Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931. === Takaoka City designated cultural properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961. * Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996. === Visitor information === ; Address * Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture ; Access * Nearest station: {{ill|lt=Echū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|WD=Q11636382|1=Etchū-Kokubu Station}} on the {{ill|lt=Himi Line|Q5357535|WD=Q5357535|1=Himi Line}} (about 15 minutes on foot) * From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|lt=Kaetsuno Bus|Q6346040|WD=Q6346040|1=Kaetsunou Bus}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya” === References === {{reflist|2}} === Further reading === * (List of Japanese-language sources) === Related items === * Other shrines claiming to be Ichinomiya of Etchū Province ** {{ill|lt=Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|WD=Q11458557|1=Imizu Shrine}} ** {{ill|lt=Takase Shrine|Q3791906|WD=Q3791906|1=Takase Shrine (Nanto)}} ** {{ill|lt=Oyama Shrine|Q11659204|WD=Q11659204|1=Oyama Shrine (Tateyama)}} === External links === {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja}} * Official website * Kokugakuin University Digital Museum {{Shinto footer}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Keta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Keta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:高岡市の神社]] [[Category:高岡市の観光地]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Etchū Province]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:富山県の旧県社]] [[Category:富山県の重要文化財]] [[Category:Cultural heritage monuments in Japan]] [[Category:Etchū Province]] [[Category:Architecture of Muromachi period]] [[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]][[Category:Move targets ∪ destinations]]
